issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee’s acquisition of occupancy rights through possession under the mortgage does not extinguish the mortgagor’s right to redeem when no legally recognized mode of extinguishment has occurred.
material_facts: The mortgagors were permanent tenants with rights in the land and mortgaged their share in it with possession.
The mortgagees were in possession of the mortgaged share because of the mortgage.
After the land was resumed, the mortgagees obtained a grant of occupancy rights based on their possession, although the mortgagors were entitled to the grant as permanent tenants.
The mortgagors had deposited the occupancy price and sought redemption.
issues.conclusion: The grant did not extinguish the mortgagors’ right to redeem the mortgage.
issues.legal_principle: A right of redemption ends only by a legally recognized means, such as agreement, merger, or a statutory provision barring redemption; otherwise, the principle is “once a mortgage, always a mortgage.” Under section 8 of the Bombay Paragana and Kulkarni Watans (Abolition) Act, 1950, tenants’ rights in the watan lands subsisted after abolition. The judgment cites no earlier cases.

rule.if: redemption_proceeding and mortgagee_in_possession and grant_derived_from_mortgage_possession and not lawful_extinguishment

predicates.redemption_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding seeking redemption of a mortgage.
predicates.mortgagee_in_possession: The mortgagee held possession of the property under the mortgage.
predicates.grant_derived_from_mortgage_possession: The mortgagee obtained a property right because possession under the mortgage enabled the grant.
predicates.lawful_extinguishment: The right to redeem was ended by agreement, merger, or a legal provision barring redemption.
predicates.redemption_right_survives: The mortgagor retains the right to redeem the mortgage.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding concerns property possessed by a mortgagee and the mortgagee’s grant derives from that possession, the redemption right survives if no lawful extinguishment occurred.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee who gains an advantage by using the position obtained under a mortgage, to the detriment of the mortgagor, must hold that advantage for the mortgagor’s benefit, subject to reimbursement of proper expenses.
material_facts: The mortgagees obtained possession of the mortgagors’ share through the mortgage.
The mortgagees obtained occupancy rights in that share because they were in possession, while the mortgagors were permanent tenants entitled to the grant.
The mortgagors had deposited the required occupancy price in time.
The mortgagees represented that they were permanent tenants, although they were mortgagees.
The redemption decree required the mortgagors to reimburse their share of the expenses incurred to secure the grant.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagees had to surrender the advantage derived from the grant for the mortgagors’ benefit, subject to payment of the proper expenses incurred in securing it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 90 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 requires a qualified owner, including a mortgagee, who uses that position to gain an advantage in derogation of another interested person’s rights to hold the advantage for that person’s benefit, subject to reimbursement of a due share of proper expenses and indemnity for proper liabilities. The Court referred to illustrations (b) and (c) to section 90 and cited no earlier cases.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding to redeem property held under a mortgage.
predicates.mortgagee_gained_advantage_through_mortg: The mortgagee used possession or another position obtained under the mortgage to gain a property advantage.
predicates.advantage_derogates_another_interested_p: The advantage gained by the mortgagee impaired the rights of another person interested in the property.
predicates.mortgagee_must_hold_advantage_for_that_p: The mortgagee must hold the advantage for the other interested person’s benefit, subject to reimbursement of that person’s due share of proper expenses.

issues.definition: If a mortgagee gains an advantage through the mortgage position and that advantage impairs another interested person’s rights, the mortgagee must hold it for that person’s benefit subject to proper expenses.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of a separate grantee does not bar relief limited to a distinct share granted to the mortgagees when the absent grantee has no interest in that share.
material_facts: The grant order allocated specified shares to the mortgagees and allocated the remaining share to another grantee.
The redemption claim concerned only the share that had been mortgaged and was granted to the mortgagees.
The absent grantee’s share was separate from the share in dispute.
issues.conclusion: The absent grantee’s non-joinder did not prevent relief concerning the mortgaged share.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the specific allocation of separate shares in the grant and the limited subject matter of the redemption decree; the absent grantee had no interest in the share at issue. No provision or earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.redemption_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding to redeem property held under a mortgage.
predicates.relief_limited_to_separately_allocated_s: The relief sought concerns only a distinct share allocated to the parties against whom relief is sought.
predicates.absent_grantee_has_no_interest_in_disput: A grantee who was not joined received a separate share and has no interest in the share at issue.
predicates.nonjoinder_does_not_bar_limited_relief: The absence of the separate grantee does not prevent relief confined to the disputed share.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding seeks relief only as to a separately allocated share in which an absent grantee has no interest, non-joinder does not bar that limited relief.
